workflow: scientist IT18 P-BIOPATHNET targeted reading (question-driven: task data, BRG, splits, interpretability method, compute cost, limitations, availability); Europe PMC JATS XML flattened per section, quotes located by exact text search; staged in the package for the integrator to record
evidence_basis: Peer-reviewed (Nature Biomedical Engineering 2026, CC BY 4.0). NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: the paper contains no WWOX, DEE or WOREE analysis.

Read in full: abstract, Main (introduction), all Results subsections including the three drug case studies and Additional examples, Table 1, Discussion with its limitations paragraph, Data and Code availability. Methods read only in part: KG completion overview, BioPathNet sections (path representation, negative sampling, BRG, training), interpretation of predictions, gene-function and drug-repurposing task construction, comparison with baselines, model evaluation; NOT read: NBFNet equations, SL and lncRNA task methods, Extended Methods. Figures: legends only (images not opened). Supplementary information not opened (per-task tables, Supplementary Fig. 5 CRY1 example).

Methods/Interpretation of prediction | 'the importance of each path is approximated by the sum of the importance of edges in that path'; Results/Case study 1 | 'the visualization highlights the ten most important paths ranked by gradient in an ad hoc pseudo-linear explanation'; Results/Overview of the different LP tasks | 'extracted from Pathway Commons59–61 encompassing ~1.8 million edges and 13 different relation types between genes and chemicals'; Methods/Gene function prediction task | 'we used the KG from the KEGG database (G1), extracted from ConsensuPathDB'; Methods/Drug repurposing task | 'we used the same data and data splits as defined by TxGNN54, reflecting a zero-shot prediction scenario'; Results/BioPathNet vs general GNN-based LP method | 'baselines such as RAGAT and NBFNet were computationally infeasible, requiring over 48 h per epoch on GPUs'; Table 1 | 'Gene function prediction0.547 ± 0.002 (0.01)'; Results/BioPathNet's performance | 'for drug repurposing, we observe a weak positive correlation (0.23), indicating a tendency of the model to associate drug indications with well-characterized drugs or diseases'; Discussion/limitations | 'it missed FDA-approved drugs such as pramiracetam, memantine and lecanemab, which were not listed in the PrimeKG database'; Discussion | 'Path embeddings capture richer context and can be interpreted more easily, but are more abstract and less intuitive for downstream tasks'; Code availability | 'The BioPathNet model and all code necessary for reproducing our results are publicly available via GitHub'; Additional examples | 'CRY1 protein in complex with → PER3 interacts with → ARNTL function of → ‘Circadian rhythm’'

Used for: the explanation method is a gradient-based local approximation (edge importance summed along paths), so a path is an influence summary, not a mechanism; gene-function task data (KEGG via ConsensusPathDB labels, Pathway Commons BRG); drug task needs PrimeKG retraining per split (no released model), GPU-scale cost; degree bias in the drug task (0.23) and hub dependence; drug performance collapses without drug-gene edges; known drugs absent from PrimeKG cannot be predicted.
